item.title: National PA Week - October 6 through 12

item.content:encoded:
WHEREAS, quality, cost-effective, and patient-centered healthcare is essential to the well-being and quality of life of all people in Maine; and


WHEREAS, physician associates/assistants (PAs) are nationally certified and state-licensed medical professionals who diagnose illnesses, develop and manage treatment plans, prescribe medications, and often serve as a patient's principal healthcare provider; and


WHEREAS, PAs are trusted providers and vital members of the healthcare team, enhancing access to high-quality care in primary care settings, hospitals, rural communities, and underserved areas; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs deliver compassionate, expert care, often serving as the first point of contact for patients and empowering individuals and families to be active participants in their own health; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs provide critical care across a broad range of medical specialties, including addressing the growing demand for behavioral and mental health services by offering compassionate, evidence-based care to individuals and families in need; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs are committed to addressing health disparities, expanding access, and providing team-based, person-centered care across every medical specialty and setting; and
 

WHEREAS, PAs have earned the respect of patients and colleagues alike for their clinical excellence, adaptability, and deep dedication to the communities they serve; and
 

WHEREAS, Maine has been a leader in progressing PA practice and ensuring access to PA services by enacting legislation in recent years to join the PA compact, change the title of the profession to accurately reflect the scope of the profession, and allow PAs to practice at the top of their education and training;


NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 6-12, 2026 as 

National PA Week

in Maine, and I encourage all residents to recognize and celebrate the important role that PAs play in improving health, advancing equity, and delivering high-quality care across the healthcare system.

In testimony whereof, I have caused

the Great Seal of the State to be

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this twenty ninth day of

September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

item.description: PRELIMINARY PRINT Volume 609 U. S. Part 1 Pages 108–140 OFFICIAL REPORTS OF THE SUPREME COURT June 23, 2026 REBECCA A. WOMELDORF reporter of decisions Page Proof Pending Publication NOTICE: This preliminary print is subject to formal revision before the bound volume is published. Users are requested to notify the Reporter of Decisions, Supreme Court of the United States, Washington, D. C. 20543, pio@supremecourt.gov, of any typographical or other formal errors. Page Proof Pending Publication 108 OCTOBER TERM, 2025 Syllabus EXXON MOBIL CORP. v. CORPORACIÓN CIMEX, S. A. (CUBA), et al. certiorari to the united states court of appeals for the district of columbia circuit No. 24–699. Argued February 23, 2026—Decided June 23, 2026 In 1960, after Fidel Castro seized power in Cuba, the Cuban Government confscated many foreign-owned assets, including Exxon's oil refnery, terminals, packaging plants, and more than a hundred service stations. Since then, two Cuban government-owned companies—Unión Cuba- Petróleo (CUPET) and Corporación CIMEX, S. A. (Cuba) (CIMEX)— have operated and profted from Exxon's expropriated assets. Exxon had no good way to sue the Cuban government entities and seek com- pensation for its confscated property until Congress passed and Presi- dent Clinton signed the Helms-Burton Act in 1996. As relevant here, the Act created a private right of action for U. S. nationals whose prop- erty was confscated by the Cuban Government against “any person that . . . traffcs in” the confscated property, 22 U. S. C. § 6082(a)(1)(A), with “person” defned to include “any agency or instrumentality of a foreign state,” § 6023(11). Exxon sued CUPET, CIMEX, and later CIMEX's Panamanian alter ego under the Helms-Burton Act in the U. S. District Court for the District of Columbia, seeking more than $1 billion in dam- ages. item.title: 806 Nonresident Individual Income Tax (PDF)
item.description:
18 DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
125 BUREAU OF REVENUE SERVICES INCOME/ESTATE TAX DIVISION
Chapter 806: NONRESIDENT INDIVIDUAL INCOME TAX
SUMMARY: This rule provides income tax guidance for nonresident individuals in the following areas:
• Determination of Maine-source income; • Deduction of Maine losses; • Attribution and apportionment of income, tax additions and tax credits to Maine; • Returns, worksheets and schedules to be used for filing; • Determination of taxable income and tax credits for spouses filing as single individuals; and • Income tax withholding obligations.
Outline of Contents:
.01 Definitions .02 Income subject to Maine income tax .03 Income not subject to Maine income tax .04 Deduction of losses .05 Special sourcing rules .06 Income tax credits .07 Return of nonresident or part-year resident individual .08 Maine taxable income computation for spouses filing as single individuals .09 Maine tax additions and tax credits for spouses filing as single individuals .10 Maine income tax withholding obligations .11 Application date
.01 Definitions. As used in this rule, unless the context otherwise indicates or may otherwise require, the following terms have the following meanings that shall apply throughout the rule.
A. Code. “Code” means the United States Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and amendments to that Code as of the date stated in 36 M.R.S. § 111(1-A).
18-125 Chapter 806 page 2
B. Intangible property. “Intangible property” means a right or possession of a nonphysical or abstract nature that has value, or a financial asset that has no intrinsic value but that represents value. Intangible property includes, but is not limited to, copyrights, patents, licenses, bills of exchange, trademarks, business books and records, business goodwill, covenants not to compete, securities, bonds, notes, insurance policies, and accounts receivable.
C. Pass

item.description: Skip First Level Navigation Skip All Navigation Maine.gov Agencies | Online Services | Help | Search Maine.gov Maine Department of Labor Contact Us | News | Online services | Publications | Sitemap Home Contact Us Online Services About MDOL News & Events Forms & Publications MDOL Bureaus Home → News & Events → Title IV PostsecondaryInstitutions: Workforce Pell Program Applications Open for Second Review Cycle Through Nov. 13 Services Jobs & Training Unemployment Insurance Disability Services Workplace Safety Labor Laws Labor Statistics Workforce Development Title IV PostsecondaryInstitutions: Workforce Pell Program Applications Open for Second Review Cycle Through Nov. 13 October 14, 2026 For Immediate Release Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist | media.dol@maine.gov AUGUSTA -The State Workforce Development Board (SWDB) is accepting applications from Title IV postsecondary institutionsseeking stateapproval to offer programs eligible for federal Workforce Pell Grants. Applications for the second review cycle are due Friday, Nov. 13 Maine's Workforce Pell application provides an online process for eligible postsecondary institutions to seek approval to offer short-term workforce training programs that meet federal Workforce Pell Grant requirements . Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly by the SWDB. Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage and in-demand careers. States are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before they are submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval. AUGUSTA -The State Workforce Development Board(SWDB) is accepting applications from Title IV postsecondary institutionsseeking stateapproval to offer programs eligible for federal Workforce Pell Grants. Applications for the second review cycle are due Friday, Nov. 13

Maine's Workforce Pell application provides an online process for eligible postsecondary institutions to seek approval to offer short-term workforce training programs that meet federal Workforce Pell Grant requirements. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly by the SWDB.

Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage and in-demand careers. States are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before they are submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state,"said Vaughan Woodruff, chair of the State Workforce Development Board."The program's support for training that connects people with skills needed for Maine's workforce presents a significant opportunity for Maine workers and employers."

The Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy establishesthe state's process foridentifying, reviewing and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. The policy was developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System and University of MaineSystem.

"Workforce Pell brings a new source of federal funding to Maine's short-term workforce training programs," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "We are excited to help Maine's postsecondary institutions take advantage of this opportunity to strengthen their programs, reach more students and prepare Maine's workforce for the future."

The SWDB will evaluate applications and make recommendations to the Governor for state certification. Programs certified by the Governor will then be submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval. Following federal approval, the SWDB will publish the list of Maine-certified Workforce Pell programs on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage within 30 days.

Institutions can find the Workforce Pell application, eligibility requirements, program guidance and additional information on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage.
